description: Figure 5 is a donut chart illustrating the distribution of deceived conversations as a percentage across two distinct levels of ambiguity: "Ambiguity 1 (Outer)" and "Ambiguity 2 (Inner)". The chart is divided into three colored segments representing the degree of deception: red for "Deceived", yellow for "Partially", and green for "Not Deceived". The outer ring, labeled "Ambiguity 1 (Outer)", shows that 67.6% of conversations were "Deceived" (red), 31.6% were "Partially" deceived (yellow), and 10.5% were "Not Deceived" (green). The inner ring, labeled "Ambiguity 2 (Inner)", displays a more granular breakdown with 57.9% "Deceived" (red), 23.5% "Partially" deceived (yellow), and 8.8% "Not Deceived" (green). A legend to the right of the chart explicitly maps each color to its corresponding deception category for both ambiguity levels. The percentages are displayed directly on the chart segments, and the overall structure visually compares the proportion of deception outcomes between the two ambiguity tiers.
